newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IPB CHARGES NOT TO AFFECT PRIVATISATION - NPF.
newsitem.headline: CZECH IPB CHARGES NOT TO AFFECT PRIVATISATION - NPF.

text.p: Plans to sell off the remainder of the Czech state's holding in Czech bank IPB a.s. should not be affected by charges against two senior IPB officials, the National Property fund (NPF) said on Tuesday.

"Because this is about people and not about IPB as an institution, the NPF does not presume that the situation which has arisen would threaten the tender for its (the NPF's) share in IPB," the NPF, the Czech privatisation agency, said in a statement.
Two, so far unnamed, officials at IPB were charged with fraud on Tuesday, investigators said. IPB's board of directors described the affair as an attempt to smear the bank's good name.
IPB is the third largest Czech bank by basic capital. The NPF holds a 31.5 percent stake in IPB and the Czech Post Office holds a further 4.5 percent, bringing the state's total holding to 36 percnt.

The state holdings should be sold off in the middle of the year and local press reports say ING Bank and Japan's Nomura are front runners on the shortlist of buyers, being drawn up by U.S based investment bank Salomon Brothers.

Czech National Bank (CNB) press spokesman Martin Svehla also refused to name the two officials. He said the CNB was following the situation closely but not preparing to take any extraordinary measures.
"We are keeping ourselves informed. The matter which is being investigated is not of an extent which could represent any danger to the bank," he told Reuters.

The NPF's statement also said that if it did not get a "satisfactory explanation" from IPB, or if the bank has not taken "sufficient measures", by next Tuesday it would call an extraordinary general meeting of IPB to "resolve personnel questions".
